    -- More precisely, we use the fact that for i in [j², (j+1)²), we have x_i ≤ x_{j²}
    -- And we can bound the sum of 1/i in this range

      -- by x_{j²} times the sum of 1/i in that range
      
      -- The crucial observation is that the sum of 1/i for i in [j², (j+1)²)
      -- is approximately log(((j+1)²)/j²) = log(1 + 2/j + 1/j²) ≈ 2/j
      
      -- So the contribution from each "square block" is roughly x_{j²} * 2/j
      -- And summing over j gives us something bounded by the constraint
      
      -- Let's use a more direct approach with the actual constraint
      have h₃ : ∀ j : ℕ, j ≥ 1 → 
        (Ico (j * j) (min ((j + 1) * (j + 1)) (k + 1))).sum (fun i => x i / (i : ℝ)) ≤

            simp only [Ico.mem] at hi
            exact hi.1
          have h₆ : i < min ((j + 1) * (j + 1)) (k + 1) := by
            simp only [Ico.mem] at hi
            exact hi.2

            intro m n hmn
            induction' hmn with m hmn IH

            · specialize hmono m

          exact h₈ i (j * j) h₇

            intro i hi
            rw [div_le_div_iff] <;> norm_cast <;>

              (try linarith [h₄ i hi]) <;>
              (try simp_all [h₄])
            <;>
            (try {
              have h₉ := h₄ i hi

                  have h₇ : (Ico (j * j) (min ((j + 1) * (j + 1)) (k + 1))).card =

        -- So the contribution from block j is at most x_{j²} * 2/j
